i find i have such a soft spot for sheldrake's morphic resonance theory not just because it has a great name but also because it's simple and makes no claims (afaik) as to any underlying mechanism which would enable it. it's a model organism of woo theories of everything.under my interpretation, it says: there is a subtle bias to all physical systems in the universe. spatiotemporal patterns which have happened before "want" to occur again.this can apparently be used to explain a wide variety of woo phenomena from telepathy to how fake cattle grids work (https://t.co/XmRj2Kc3du). the idea is that this subtle bias is strong enough that brain states in one organism would develop similarity to brain states from other (similar) organisms be they contemporaneous or from the past, and so their internal states and patterns of behaviour would develop similarities too. like magical nonlocal canalisation. (you would expect to see these dynamics more in systems with dynamics close to criticality)to what extent is this theory equivalent to saying, "a wizard did it"? if it can explain anything doesn't it also explain nothing? what's the negative space – are there any woo phenomena which you *couldn't* explain using morphic resonance?

The discourse is constructive rather than dialectical—participants are not debating whether woo is valid, but *how* to integrate it into coherent frameworks. The boundary object is the concept of 'woo' itself as a placeholder for phenomena that resist current scientific explanation. The arc moves from: (1) Pre-context warnings about pop science causing harm (2020), (2) Recognition that metaphysical explanations can be useful even when factually incorrect (2022), (3) The viral catalyst tweet validating woo (2024), (4) Proliferation of practical frameworks (morphic resonance, pluralism, group mind phenomena), and (5) Contemporary synthesis arguing science is 'historically obedient' and late to reality (2025). High cohesion around shared vocabulary ('the mystery,' 'pluralism,' 'boundary objects'), medium-high evolution as ideas shift from defensive justification to confident application, and high utility for practitioners seeking legitimacy for non-rational knowledge systems.
